page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a High Performance family virtual server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor. The system is configured with 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 180 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU allocation is shared, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core capabilities but constrained multi-core performance. The server achieved an average score of 1450.08 in stress-ng single-core CPU testing, while its multi-core stress-ng performance of 5759.17 falls into the lower tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a strong cached read speed of 416.34 GB/sec for small blocks, but large-block uncached reads drop to 33.43 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show weaker performance, with a Passmark encryption score of 2160.1 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.43 GB/sec. However, Redis SET operations perform well, reaching 6.06 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory-to-core ratio, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring NVMe storage but not sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU resource, which limits multi-threaded scaling, as evidenced by the weak multi-core Geekbench score of 3411.0 and poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. This configuration is best suited for lightweight web serving, Redis caching, basic text processing, and development environments rather than heavy database operations, parallel software compilation, or large-scale data processing.
